title: the house root reads its editable install's file URL as a path
intention: The house root is the path the editable install's file URL names, decoded as a file URL on every platform.
why: Law 7: a diagnostic that names a path which does not exist hides the real one; and the house's own client must be able to replace its own stale bus. Measured 2026-11-14 on akiendell (Windows) at origin/main d6bebdfb7: direct_url.json holds file:///C:/automation/local/cairn; remote._house_root() answered C:\C:\automation\local\cairn against _CLASS_ROOT C:\automation\local\cairn (equal False), because url.removeprefix('file://') leaves '/C:/...'. So every client on Windows, the house's own included, is refused a replace of a stale live bus (3deafc9e36de), and BusStale names a path that does not exist. cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_a_foreign_root_refuses_a_stale_live_bus.py tooth 1 reds on Windows on main: '/nonexistent/...' resolves to 'C:\nonexistent\...'.
traces_to: Law 7; ticket 3deafc9e36de (the refusal this root gates)
how: D1: THE DECODE. cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py _house_root reads the URL with urllib.parse.urlparse + urllib.request.url2pathname (which also decodes %XX), then resolves. D2: PROOFS. cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_the_house_root_reads_its_file_url_as_a_path.py: the box's own checkout as Path.as_uri() reads back as itself; a scratch dir named with a space reads back with the space. D3: THE FIXTURE. cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_a_foreign_root_refuses_a_stale_live_bus.py tooth 1 looks for the house root as resolved, so it holds on Windows.

clauses.claim: an editable install whose URL is this checkout's own Path.as_uri() gives _house_root() == that checkout's resolved path, on Windows and Linux
a house root whose name holds a space reads back with the space, not %20
cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_a_foreign_root_refuses_a_stale_live_bus.py tooth 1 is green on Windows and Linux, and its other teeth are unchanged
